key_insight: PHO-Agents combines structured EHR modeling with multiple LLM-based medical agents to improve health outcome prediction and generate more interpretable explanations.
clinical_relevance: This hybrid approach could support clinical decision support by better predicting risks such as mortality, AKI onset, and immune-related adverse events while providing human-readable rationale.
method: Encodes longitudinal structured EHR data into patient representations and initial prediction logits.
Uses a data agent to turn EHR signals into patient summaries, then retrieves relevant clinical guidelines.
Employs research and doctor agents plus a leader agent to synthesize reasoning; merges LLM outputs with EHR model predictions.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on three real-world cohorts and outperformed single-agent and multi-agent LLM baselines, including a PR-AUC of 90.20 ± 2.07 for AKI in-hospital mortality versus 56.46 ± 2.98 for the best single-agent baseline.
watch_item: Performance was shown in retrospective cohort evaluations, so real-world deployment would still need prospective validation, workflow testing, and careful monitoring for model drift or guideline mismatch.
paper_title: PHO-Agents: A Large Language Model Powered Multi-Agent System for Predicting Health Outcomes
